blueprints.name: SaaS subscription workspace
blueprints.tagline: Teams, roles, plans, and billing webhooks that cannot double-charge.
blueprints.problem: Build a multi-tenant product where customers create a workspace, invite teammates, choose a paid plan, and manage billing. The hard parts are tenant isolation, role changes, webhook reliability, and keeping authorisation aligned with subscription state.
blueprints.stack_notes: Django + PostgreSQL + Redis cache/queue. A billing provider such as Stripe for checkout and webhooks. Use a background worker for email and reconciliation. Postgres row-level security is optional but valuable at scale.

Landing / pricing
Sign up → create workspace
Workspace dashboard
Members and invite flow
Billing and invoices
Provider checkout return
Provider webhook (no browser session)
Audit log / danger zone

accounts — user, workspace, membership, invitations
billing — plan, subscription, provider events, invoices
core — tenant middleware, permissions, audit events
notifications — email and in-app notifications
config — settings by environment
infrastructure — tasks, cache, storage
blueprints.models_code:
class Workspace(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    slug = models.SlugField(unique=True)
    plan = models.ForeignKey("billing.Plan", on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

class Membership(models.Model):
    class Role(models.TextChoices):
        OWNER = "owner", "Owner"
        ADMIN = "admin", "Admin"
        MEMBER = "member", "Member"
    workspace = models.ForeignKey(Workspace, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="members")
    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    role = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=Role.choices)
    class Meta:
        constraints = [
            models.UniqueConstraint(fields=["workspace", "user"], name="unique_workspace_member")
        ]

class Subscription(models.Model):
    workspace = models.OneToOneField(Workspace, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    provider_customer_id = models.CharField(max_length=120, unique=True)
    price_id = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=30)
    current_period_end = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    cancel_at_period_end = models.BooleanField(default=False)

class ProviderEvent(models.Model):
    event_id = models.CharField(max_length=120, unique=True)
    event_type = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    received_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    processed_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
blueprints.checklist:
Create workspace and membership in one transaction.
Resolve tenant from the authenticated user, never from a client-supplied ID.
Scope every queryset by workspace.
Define role capabilities in one policy module and test each role.
Integrate checkout with server-side plan/price mapping.
Verify webhook signatures on the raw body and deduplicate event IDs.
Reconcile provider subscription state on a schedule.
Add audit events for role changes, billing changes, and deletions.
Implement invite expiry and single-use tokens.
Add per-tenant quotas and rate limits before launch.
blueprints.pitfalls:
Trusting a workspace_id from the browser.
Giving every staff user superuser access.
Letting the frontend decide the price or plan.
Handling billing webhooks without signature verification or idempotency.
Sending email inside the request transaction.
Forgetting to revoke sessions/invites when a member is removed.

blueprints.name: Two-sided marketplace
blueprints.tagline: Listings, orders, payouts, and reviews with money-safe state transitions.
blueprints.problem: Build a marketplace where sellers list inventory and buyers purchase it. The domain is deceptively complex: inventory reservation, fees, refunds, payouts, reviews, search, and disputes all have different consistency requirements.
blueprints.stack_notes: Django + PostgreSQL. Object storage for listing images, a search index or Postgres full-text search, a queue for notifications/payouts, and a payment provider that supports separate charges/transfers or connected accounts.

class Listing(models.Model):

class Order(models.Model):

    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, default="pending")
    total_cents = models.PositiveIntegerField()

class OrderLine(models.Model):
    order = models.ForeignKey(Order, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="lines")

class LedgerEntry(models.Model):
    order = models.ForeignKey(Order, on_delete=models.PROTECT)

blueprints.starter_code:
@transaction.atomic
def place_order(buyer, listing_id, quantity, idempotency_key):
    existing = Order.objects.filter(
        buyer=buyer, idempotency_key=idempotency_key
    ).first()
    if existing:
        return existing

    listing = Listing.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=listing_id)
    if listing.stock < quantity:
        raise ValidationError("Not enough stock")

    total = listing.price_cents * quantity
    order = Order.objects.create(
        buyer=buyer,
        total_cents=total,
        currency=listing.currency,
        idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
    )
    OrderLine.objects.create(
        order=order,
        listing=listing,
        quantity=quantity,
        unit_price_cents=listing.price_cents,
    )
    listing.stock = F("stock") - quantity
    listing.save(update_fields=["stock"])
    OutboxEvent.objects.create(
        topic="order.created",
        payload={"order_id": order.pk},
    )
    return order
blueprints.checklist:
Separate buyers and sellers as roles or profiles, not two user tables.
Store money as integer minor units and an explicit currency.
Reserve stock transactionally or model reservations explicitly.
Use idempotency keys for checkout and provider webhooks.
Record every financial movement in an append-only ledger.
Model refunds and disputes as state machines, not free-form status edits.
Only allow reviews after a completed order.
Make seller payouts a background, auditable process.
Index search fields and paginate deterministically.
Plan moderation, abuse reporting, and tax responsibilities early.
blueprints.pitfalls:
Using floats for money.
Decrementing stock without a transaction or constraint.
Trusting client-supplied prices.
Letting a webhook and a redirect both mark an order paid.
Editing order totals after payment without a ledger entry.
Building search as an unbounded icontains query on every request.

blueprints.name: Booking & scheduling system
blueprints.tagline: Availability, time zones, deposits, and no double bookings.
blueprints.problem: Build a service where customers book a resource such as a room, clinician, or equipment slot. Calendar correctness, time zones, cancellation windows, deposits, and concurrency are the real work.
blueprints.stack_notes: Django + PostgreSQL. Store UTC instants; render in the resource/customer time zone. For overlap protection use a database constraint or serialized transaction, not a Python-only check. Payments and reminders can be background tasks.

Booking form and confirmation
Deposit/payment step
Customer booking management

catalog — service, resource, duration, buffer
scheduling — availability rule, exception, booking
payments — deposit, refund, provider events
notifications — confirmation and reminders
staff — schedule management and permissions
blueprints.models_code:
class Resource(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    timezone = models.CharField(max_length=64, default="UTC")
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)

class AvailabilityRule(models.Model):
    resource = models.ForeignKey(Resource, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    weekday = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField()  # 0=Monday
    start_time = models.TimeField()
    end_time = models.TimeField()

class Booking(models.Model):
    resource = models.ForeignKey(Resource, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    customer = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    start_at = models.DateTimeField()  # UTC
    end_at = models.DateTimeField()    # UTC
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, default="pending")
    deposit_cents = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=0)
    idempotency_key = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    class Meta:
        indexes = [
            models.Index(fields=["resource", "start_at"], name="booking_resource_start_idx")
        ]
blueprints.starter_code:
@transaction.atomic
def create_booking(resource, customer, start_at, end_at, idempotency_key):
    if start_at >= end_at:
        raise ValidationError("End must be after start")

    existing = Booking.objects.filter(
        customer=customer, idempotency_key=idempotency_key
    ).first()
    if existing:
        return existing

    # Serialize bookings for this resource; the DB constraint remains the backstop.
    Resource.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=resource.pk)
    overlap = Booking.objects.filter(
        resource=resource,
        status__in=["pending", "confirmed"],
        start_at__lt=end_at,
        end_at__gt=start_at,
    ).exists()
    if overlap:
        raise ValidationError("That slot was just taken")

    booking = Booking.objects.create(
        resource=resource,
        customer=customer,
        start_at=start_at,
        end_at=end_at,
        idempotency_key=idempotency_key,
    )
    transaction.on_commit(lambda: send_booking_email.enqueue(booking.pk))
    return booking
blueprints.checklist:
Store UTC and convert at the edges; display the resource time zone.
Define buffers and service durations explicitly.
Model recurring availability plus date-specific exceptions/holidays.
Protect overlaps with a database-level constraint where supported.
Lock or serialize the resource during the booking write.
Use idempotency keys for double-clicked confirmations.
Make cancellation and reschedule explicit state transitions.
Expire unpaid holds and release inventory.
Send reminders via a retryable task, not the request.
Test DST transitions and midnight boundaries.
blueprints.pitfalls:
Comparing naive local datetimes.
Trusting the browser's time zone without validation.
Checking overlap in Python without a transaction or DB constraint.
Forgetting appointment buffers and cleanup time.
Allowing an unpaid pending booking to block a slot forever.
Using a unique constraint on start_at only; it does not prevent overlap.

blueprints.name: Editorial CMS & publishing workflow
blueprints.tagline: Drafts, revisions, previews, and a publish button with an audit trail.
blueprints.problem: Build a content platform for writers and editors. The public site needs fast published reads, while the newsroom needs drafts, scheduled publishing, previews, revisions, and safe rollbacks without exposing unpublished content.
blueprints.stack_notes: Django + PostgreSQL for content and revisions. Object storage/CDN for media. Cache published pages and invalidate on publish. A background task for scheduling and social/email fan-out.
blueprints.screens:
Article list / workspace
Rich article editor
Preview as a specific audience
Revision history and diff
Editorial review / approval
Scheduled publish queue
Public article page
SEO metadata and redirects
blueprints.structure:
content — article, revision, category, tag
workflow — draft, review, approved, published, archived
public — published-only views, feeds, sitemap
media — images and renditions
search — published search index
audit — editorial actions
blueprints.models_code:
class Article(models.Model):
    class Status(models.TextChoices):
        DRAFT = "draft", "Draft"
        REVIEW = "review", "In review"
        PUBLISHED = "published", "Published"
        ARCHIVED = "archived", "Archived"
    slug = models.SlugField(unique=True)
    title = models.CharField(max_length=240)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=Status.choices, default=Status.DRAFT)
    published_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

class Revision(models.Model):
    article = models.ForeignKey(Article, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="revisions")
    title = models.CharField(max_length=240)
    body = models.TextField()
    created_by = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    note = models.CharField(max_length=240, blank=True)

class Category(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=80)
    slug = models.SlugField(unique=True)

class ArticleCategory(models.Model):
    article = models.ForeignKey(Article, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    category = models.ForeignKey(Category, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    class Meta:
        constraints = [
            models.UniqueConstraint(fields=["article", "category"], name="unique_article_category")
        ]
blueprints.checklist:
Keep public and editorial views separate.
Filter public queries by published status and published_at.
Create a revision on every meaningful save or publish.
Implement preview tokens that expire and never index.
Define who can draft, review, publish, and archive.
Schedule publishing with a task and a published_at gate.
Invalidate caches and feeds on publish/unpublish.
Add redirects for slug changes and a sitemap.
Strip unsafe HTML or sanitize rich text server-side.
Back up content and test restore.
blueprints.pitfalls:
Letting unpublished drafts appear in search or sitemaps.
Trusting client-side rich-text sanitisation only.
Editing published content without a revision.
Publishing by changing a boolean with no timestamp or audit.
Invalidating the entire cache on every keystroke.
Treating staff authors as superusers.

blueprints.name: Customer support desk
blueprints.tagline: Tickets, conversations, attachments, and SLAs without email chaos.
blueprints.problem: Build an internal support tool that turns email/chat/form messages into tracked tickets with assignments, priorities, internal notes, attachments, and SLA timers. Inbound email parsing and permissions are the sharp edges.
blueprints.stack_notes: Django + PostgreSQL. Inbound email via a provider webhook, background tasks for notifications, object storage for attachments, and a search index. Consider a separate staff/admin host and SSO.

Inbox / queue
Ticket detail with conversation
Assignment and priority

Attachment viewer
SLA / waiting states
Customer and organisation profile
Reporting dashboard

tickets — ticket, message, attachment, tag
organisations — customer account, contact
routing — queues, assignment rules, SLA
inbound — email/chat webhook normalization
notifications — agent/customer messaging
reporting — response and resolution metrics
blueprints.models_code:
class Ticket(models.Model):
    class Status(models.TextChoices):
        NEW = "new", "New"
        OPEN = "open", "Open"
        WAITING = "waiting", "Waiting on customer"
        RESOLVED = "resolved", "Resolved"
        CLOSED = "closed", "Closed"
    organisation = models.ForeignKey("orgs.Organisation", on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    requester = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    subject = models.CharField(max_length=240)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=Status.choices, default=Status.NEW)
    priority = models.CharField(max_length=20, default="normal")
    assignee = models.ForeignKey(
        settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, null=True, blank=True,
        on_delete=models.SET_NULL, related_name="assigned_tickets"
    )
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

class Message(models.Model):
    ticket = models.ForeignKey(Ticket, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="messages")
    author = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    body = models.TextField()
    is_internal = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

class Attachment(models.Model):
    message = models.ForeignKey(Message, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="attachments")
    file = models.FileField(upload_to="support/%Y/%m/")
    original_name = models.CharField(max_length=255)
    content_type = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    size = models.PositiveIntegerField()
blueprints.checklist:
Verify inbound provider signatures and deduplicate event IDs.
Thread replies by ticket token or provider thread ID, not subject guessing.
Separate internal notes from customer-visible messages.
Sanitize inbound HTML and never execute attachments.
Store attachments privately with safe names and malware scanning.
Use assignment rules and explicit SLA states.
Send customer email after commit, with retries.
Add full-text search over tickets and messages.
Audit access to sensitive customer data.
Measure first response, resolution, and reopen rates.
blueprints.pitfalls:
Reply-to spoofing and accepting unsigned inbound mail.
Trusting HTML email bodies.
Letting agents see every tenant/customer.
Sending internal notes to customers.
Blocking the webhook while processing attachments.
Using subject lines as the only threading key.

blueprints.name: Mobile app API backend
blueprints.tagline: Versioned JSON, token auth, pagination, and offline-friendly contracts.
blueprints.problem: Build the backend for iOS/Android clients that cannot be redeployed instantly. You need stable API contracts, token auth, pagination, idempotent writes, push notifications, and a deprecation strategy.
blueprints.stack_notes: Django + DRF + PostgreSQL. Token/JWT auth through a trusted library, Redis for throttles/cache, object storage for media, and APNs/FCM for push. Consider OpenAPI schema generation and contract tests.

Home feed
Detail screen
Create/edit flow
Upload media
Push notification handling
Account and devices
Force-upgrade / maintenance states

api — versioned serializers, viewsets, routers
accounts — user, device, refresh token family
content — posts, media, feed
notifications — device token, push job
common — pagination, errors, idempotency
schema — OpenAPI and contract tests

    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    idempotency_key = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    endpoint = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    response_status = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField()
    response_body = models.JSONField()
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    class Meta:
        constraints = [
            models.UniqueConstraint(
                fields=["user", "idempotency_key"],
                name="unique_mobile_write_key",
            )
        ]
blueprints.checklist:
Version the contract from day one; never silently rename fields.
Use short-lived access tokens and rotating refresh tokens.
Scope every queryset to the authenticated user/tenant.
Use cursor pagination for feeds.
Support idempotency keys for create/payment actions.
Return structured errors with stable codes.
Document with OpenAPI and test the schema.
Handle app-version gating and maintenance modes.
Store push tokens per device and remove invalid tokens.
Plan media upload limits and background processing.
blueprints.pitfalls:
Assuming all clients update together.
Exposing sequential IDs where enumeration matters.
Putting long-lived secrets in the mobile app.
Using page-number pagination for a shifting feed.
Returning raw stack traces in API errors.
Forgetting token revocation on password reset or device loss.
